Auger, DeBlois & Lambert (2025) DBH–height models for Québec plantations

Source: R/hd_auger2025.R
hd_auger2025.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the DBH–height relationships of Auger, DeBlois and Lambert (2025; Avis technique SSS-10) for black spruce and jack pine plantations in Québec. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm) alone, or from DBH and a plot-level predictor: the plot mean DBH, or the dominant height and dominant DBH.

Usage

hd_auger2025(
  DBH,
  species,
  variant = c("dbh", "plot_mean_dbh", "dominant"),
  DMEAN = NULL,
  HDOM = NULL,
  DDOM = NULL,
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be > 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes, "PICE.MAR" or "PINU.BAN" (compact "PICEMAR" is accepted).

variant

Model variant: "dbh" (default), "plot_mean_dbh" or "dominant". See Details.

DMEAN

Numeric vector. Plot level. Arithmetic mean DBH (cm) of the plot, used by variant = "plot_mean_dbh": "le DHP moyen de tous les arbres de la placette" (source "DMOY", p. 6), i.e. the arithmetic (not quadratic) mean DBH of all trees in the plot. The source does not state whether natural ingress is included or a minimum DBH. Must be >= 0.

HDOM

Numeric vector. Plot level. Dominant height (m), used by variant = "dominant": mean height of the dominant trees of the plot (source "HDOM", p. 7), the dominant trees being "les 8 plus hauts arbres plantés faisant partie de l'étage des arbres dominants et bien répartis dans la placette (200 arbres/ha)" (400 m² plots, p. 2). Must be > 0.

DDOM

Numeric vector. Plot level. Mean DBH (cm) of the same dominant trees (source "DDOM", p. 7), used by variant = "dominant". Must be >= 0.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("auger2025_dbh", "auger2025_plot_mean_dbh" or "auger2025_dominant").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope: black spruce (PICE.MAR, source "EPN") and jack pine (PINU.BAN, source "PIG") in monospecific plantations of the Québec plantation monitoring network (p. 2). The models were not fitted to natural stands; stand origin cannot be checked by the function.

Variants (chosen with variant):

"dbh" (default)

Korf form, eq. 10 (Tableau 7, p. 11), both species: $$H = 1.3 + \alpha_1 \exp(-\alpha_2 DBH^{-\alpha_3}).$$ Estimates the mean height of the population for a given DBH; the authors note that its shape is unlikely to suit any particular plot (pp. 4–5).

"plot_mean_dbh"

Requires DMEAN. Jack pine, eq. 11 (Chapman–Richards) and black spruce, eq. 12 (Hossfeld II) (Tableau 8, p. 14): $$PIG: H = 1.3 + (\alpha_{10} + \alpha_{11} MD) [1 - \exp(-(\alpha_{20} + \alpha_{21} MD) DBH)]^{\alpha_3};$$ $$EPN: H = 1.3 + (\alpha_{10} + \alpha_{11} MD) \frac{DBH^{\alpha_3}}{(\alpha_{20} + \alpha_{21} MD) + DBH^{\alpha_3}},$$ where \(MD\) is DMEAN.

"dominant"

Requires HDOM and DDOM. Jack pine, eq. 13 and black spruce, eq. 14 (Tableau 9, p. 17), the same forms with \(\alpha_{10} + \alpha_{11} HDOM\) as asymptote term and \(\alpha_{20} + \alpha_{22} DD\) as rate/scale term, where \(DD\) is DDOM.

Predictors not used by the selected variant are ignored with a warning.

Height convention: total tree height; DBH is measured at 1.3 m and every form tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Fit: weighted fixed-effects nonlinear regressions; a plot random effect did not improve the fit and none was included (pp. 5–7), so the published coefficients are used directly. Variance-function parameters are not used.

Korf asymptote: the published \(\alpha_1\) values are very large (1,630,094 m for jack pine and 101,489 m for black spruce), so the "dbh" curves keep increasing beyond the data. Extrapolation beyond the calibration DBH range is not recommended.

Rows with NA in any used input return NA height. Inputs outside the per-species calibration ranges (Tableau 1, p. 4: DBH and, depending on the variant, mean DBH, dominant height and dominant DBH) are computed and reported in a single warning.

No worked example or table of predicted heights is published; the implementation is checked for plausibility only (see data-raw/Auger2025_model-spec.md).

References

Auger, I., DeBlois, J., and Lambert, M.-C. (2025). Relations hauteur-diamètre, tarifs de cubage et équations de défilement pour l'épinette noire et le pin gris en plantation au Québec. Gouvernement du Québec, ministère des Ressources naturelles et des Forêts, Direction de la recherche forestière. Avis technique SSS-10. 31 p. doi:10.82204/dcwg-5v65

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# DBH only (Korf)
hd_auger2025(DBH = c(5, 10, 20), species = c("PICE.MAR", "PINU.BAN", "PINU.BAN"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   4.34
#> 2   7.77
#> 3  15.0 

# With the plot mean DBH
hd_auger2025(
  DBH = c(5, 10, 20), species = "PINU.BAN",
  variant = "plot_mean_dbh", DMEAN = 12
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   6.31
#> 2   9.49
#> 3  13.0 

# With dominant height and dominant DBH, inside dplyr::mutate()
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(6, 9, 12),
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  HDOM = 9, DDOM = 11
)
dplyr::mutate(
  trees,
  hd_auger2025(DBH, species, variant = "dominant",
               HDOM = HDOM, DDOM = DDOM,
               keep_model_id = TRUE)
)
#>   DBH  species HDOM DDOM   height           model_id
#> 1   6 PICE.MAR    9   11 6.152723 auger2025_dominant
#> 2   9 PICE.MAR    9   11 7.731378 auger2025_dominant
#> 3  12 PICE.MAR    9   11 8.704548 auger2025_dominant
